exports.source: file line 30, Tientsin Native Customs II. Exports, 1905 column
exports.note: The row in No. 146 (name garbled 'Satpetre') reads '328 591 ,6365' under the 1902-1905 columns, i.e. 328 / 59 / 1,263 / 65[4]. The 1905 comparison column of No. 154 reads 654, so 654 is entered. Junk-borne native trade from Taku and Peitang; destination not named.

issue_notes: No. 146 (1905 Q2): Tientsin Native Customs saltpetre export corrected from 65 to 654 and Kowloon saltpetre (11,400 piculs) added, both from the comparison columns of No. 154. Kowloon sulphur for this quarter is still unknown. Month headings misread as 'Arms' are not arms trade.
